result_text:
Any folder whose name starts with `mock` or `__mock` now counts as mock resources, whatever follows. That covers plain `mock`, `mock.data`, `mock(old)`, `mock-größe` and `mock模拟`, at any depth and in backslash paths. The new test passes.

**Change:** in `codeanalyzer/src/main/java/nl/obren/sokrates/sourcecode/scoping/ScopingConventions.java`, I replaced the folder-name character class `[a-zA-Z0-9_\- ]+` in the two mock rules with `[^/\\]*`. That class required at least one more ASCII character after `mock`, which is why plain `mock/` and the punctuation and non-ASCII names slipped through. The new pattern stays inside one folder name.

**Test:** I added `MockFolderConventionTest` under `codeanalyzer/src/test/java/nl/obren/sokrates/sourcecode/scoping/`. It checks both the new cases and the old ones (`mocks`, `__mocks__`, `mock-data`, `mock_data`, `mock data`, `mockStore`) with `/` and `\` paths. It also checks that `remock/`, `demo/`, `src/main/java/`, `mock.java` and `mockery.java` are not classified as test code.

I only ran that one test class, not the rest of the module's tests.
